newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Anglo American Corp's control of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) has slipped over the past five months while black business and "mini-conglomerates" continue to consolidate their positions.

- A new public company, to be listed on the JSE this year, will be set up to run horse racing in Gauteng in an attempt to manage the industry on "commercial lines", provincial finance and economic MEC Jabu Moleketi said.

- JCI Ltd's gold division has reported on of its sharpest quarter-on-quarter collapses, with taxed profit before capex slumping two-thirds following a lower average gold price and poor operational performances at its two profit driving mines.
- The Reserve Bank's net oversold position on its forward book had fallen by $1 billion by March 31 and was expected to fall further as confidence in the rand increased, governor Chris Stals said.
- The finance department is investigating the economic impact of levies proposed by different government departments and will prepare a cabinet memorandum on the issue in the next couple of months.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The tightly held South African Druggists' share price lost five percent, or 200 cents, to 40 rand on Tuesday on speculation that it was likely to be sold to an Arab consortium for $600 million, sources close to the pharmaceutical group in Malbak Ltd's stable said.

- JCI, the country's first controlled mining house, has suffered a huge fall in its profitability this quarter as the depressed bullion price, extended Christmas holidays and geological problems combined to hit earnings.

- Hilton International, the worldwide hotel chain, is planning to open a new chain of three-star hotels in 15 South African cities as part of a multi-million-rand investment programme in this country, Raymond Chigot, the chain's vice president for corporate development, said on Tuesday.
- The money market shortage, an important indicator of the direction of interest rates, hit a six-month low of 6,743 billion rand on Monday, according to Reserve Bank date released on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD
- Anglo American's control came to a close at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

- The South African government is considering the possibility of allowing ordinary investors to buy shares in the Telkom telecommunications network which could lead to the company's listing on the JSE.
THE STAR
- Peruvian police say forces who stormed the rebel-held Japanese ambassador's residence late Wednesday night South African time have slain all the rebels while rescuing their hostages.
- Johannesburg police have arrested more than 800 people, including the leader of a notorious syndicate, since President Nelson Mandela announced his crime crackdown in Parliament last Tuesday.

- A birth control initiative intended to limit the elephant population in the Kruger National Park has gone awry: Far from limiting the elephant cows' fertility, the hormone they have been injected with has left them permanently on heat. The six- month-olf project has now been shelved.

- Senior African National Congress members are preparing amnesty applications for their part in the Magoo's Bar bombing and other "special operations" following evidence given to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission by former Umkhonto we Sizwe cadre Robert McBride.

- Independent Broadcasting Authority councillors have rounded on IBA chief executive officer Harris Gxaweni, accusing him of being ultimately responsible for financial malpractices which councillors are alleged to have committed with government issued credit cards.
